<p align="center">
floating gui library for the web

<br><a align="center" href="https://gooey.braebo.dev">gooey.braebo.dev</a>

</p>

Gooey is designed for creating interactive control panels that work seamlessly in both development and production environments. Use it for creative coding, data visualization, interactive art, educational demos, WebGL experiments, and any web experience where users need real-time parameter control.

<blockquote>
  <h6>🚧 Pre <code>v1.0.0</code></h6>
  Changes are frequent and breaking 𛱠
</blockquote>

<br>

## Features

<p align="center">

&nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp;&nbsp; Preset Manager &nbsp;&nbsp; · &nbsp; Theme Manager &nbsp;&nbsp; · &nbsp; Draggable / Resizable / Placeable &nbsp;&nbsp; · &nbsp; Local Storage Integration &nbsp;&nbsp; · &nbsp; Generators &nbsp;&nbsp; · &nbsp; Reset Mechanism &nbsp;&nbsp; · &nbsp; Undo/Redo History &nbsp;&nbsp; · &nbsp; Flexible API &nbsp;&nbsp; · &nbsp; Fully Typed &nbsp;&nbsp; · &nbsp; Zero Dependencies

</p>

<br>

## Getting Started

### 1. Install

```elixir
npm install gooey
```

```typescript
import { Gooey } from 'gooey'
```

<details><summary>More Install Methods</summary>
<br>
<!-- Alternatives-->
<!-- There are a few other ways to install `gooey`, most of which I recommend over NPM: -->

<!-- <br> -->

<details><summary>JSR</summary>

<a href="https://jsr.io">JSR</a> is a modern alternative to NPM

```elixir
npx jsr add @braebo/gooey
```

```typescript
import { Gooey } from '@braebo/gooey'
```

<br>
</details>

<details><summary>PNPM</summary>

<a href="https://pnpm.io">PNPM</a> is the recommended way to install `gooey`.

```elixir
pnpm i -D gooey
```

```typescript
import { Gooey } from 'gooey'
```

<br>
</details>

<details><summary>CDN</summary>

```html
<script type="module">
	import { Gooey } from 'https://esm.sh/gooey'

	const gui = new Gooey()
</script>
```

</details>

</details>

### 2. Create a new `Gooey`

```typescript
const gui = new Gooey()
```

<br>

## Basics

Use [`add`](#add) to create a new [input](#inputs)

```typescript
gooey.add('hello', 'world')

gooey.add('count', 1, { min: -1 })
```

<br>

Use [`addMany`](#addmany) to create multiple inputs at once:

```typescript
gooey.addMany({
	stuff: true,
	more_stuff: {
		like_colors: '#4aa7ff' as const,
		or_buttons: () => alert('thanks!'),
	},
})
```

<br>

<!-- events - `on` method -->

Do stuff [`on`](#on) change:

```typescript
const greetingInput = gooey.add('greeting', 'hello')

greetingInput.on('change', console.log) // logs the text value when changed
```

<details><summary><em><sup>alternatives</sup></em></summary>

The `onChange` option can also be used to set a callback that will be called when the value changes:

```typescript
gooey.add('title', 'change me', {
	onChange: v => (gooey.title = v),
})
```

Or, you can chain stuff:

```typescript
gooey.add('title', 'change me').on('change', v => (gooey.title = v))
```

</details>

<br>

<!-- bind - `bind` method -->

Instead of using [`add`](#add) with event callbacks, you can use [`bind`](#bind) to automatically sync an object's values with an input. For example:

```typescript
const data = {
	size: 12,
	color: '#4aa7ff' as const,
}

gooey.bind(data, 'size')
gooey.bind(data, 'color')
```

<br>

<!-- bindMany - `bindMany` method -->

Bind to an entire object with [`bindMany`](#bindmany)

```typescript
const data = {
	wght: 100,
	wdth: 75,
}

gooey.bindMany(data)
```

<!-- todo - these details should move to the `bindMany` section -->

<!-- <details><summary><sup>more info</sup></summary>

You can also pass options to `bindMany`:

```typescript
const data = {
    wght: 300,
    wdth: 100,
}

gooey.bindMany(data, {
    wght: { min: 100, max: 900 },
    wdth: { min: 100, max: 130 },
})
```

The types here will be inferred for all that intellisense goodness.

</details> -->

<br>

Create [folders](#folders) with `addFolder`

```typescript
const outer = gooey.addFolder('outer')

const inner = outer.addFolder('inner')

inner.add('say sike', () => outer.close(), {
	text: 'sike',
})
```

<!-- todo - these details should move to the `Folder` section -->

<!-- <details><summary>Pro tip &nbsp;·&nbsp; click folder headers to open / close them</summary>

The `closed` state can be persisted in `localStorage`:

```typescript
// Persist all states
const gooey = new Gooey({ storage: true })

// Only `closed` state
const gooey = new Gooey({
    storage: {
        closed: true,
    },
})
```

</details> -->

## Inputs

<details><summary>Inputs Table</summary><br>

| Status | Feature    | Primitive                      |
| ------ | ---------- | ------------------------------ |
| ✅     | Number     | `number`                       |
| ✅     | Text       | `string`                       |
| ✅     | Switch     | `boolean`                      |
| ✅     | Select     | `Array<any>`                   |
| ✅     | Button     | `{ text, onClick, ... }`       |
| ✅     | ButtonGrid | `{ text, onClick, ... }[][]`   |
| ✅     | Color      | `Color \| ColorRepresentation` |
| 🏗️     | Range      | `{ min, max }`                 |
| 🏗️     | Vector2    | `{ x, y }`                     |
| 🏗️     | Vector3    | `{ x, y, z }`                  |

</details>

<br>

### `add` vs `bind`

There are two ways to create inputs; [`add`](#add) or [`bind`](#bind) _(along with [`addMany`](#addmany) / [`bindMany`](#bindmany) for multiple inputs)_. The return value will be the generated `Input` instance.

-   [`add`](#add) inputs when you have no data and just want to generate some values and hook into change [events](#events). The value will be created and managed by Gooey.

-   [`bind`](#bind) inputs when you have an existing object, and you want its value(s) to stay in sync with the generated input(s) automatically. This is useful for data that's integrated into a larger system, like reactive state in a web app or entities in a 3D scene graph.

<br>

### `add`

The `Folder.add` method can be used to create any input.

```typescript
type add = <T>(
  title: string,
  initialValue: T,
  options?: InputOptions<T>
): Input<T>
```

It accepts a `title`, `initialValue`, and `options` object.

> [!TIP]
> Passing an empty string as the `title` will omit the title's `<div>` element, allowing the input to fill the entire width of the parent folder.

<br>

The type of input generated depends on the type of the `initialValue` argument. For example, passing a `string` results in an `InputText` instance, while passing a `number` results in an `InputNumber` instance.

```typescript
gooey.add('my text', 'foo') // string -> InputText

gooey.add('my number', 1) // number -> InputNumber
```

<details><summary>All <code>add</code> overloads</summary>

Simple examples of each type of input that can be created with the `add` method _(with empty strings in the `title` arguments for simplicity)_:

```typescript
// InputText
gooey.add('', 'foo') // string

// InputNumber
gooey.add('', 1) // number

// InputColor
gooey.add('', '#4aa7ff') // ColorValue

// InputSelect
gooey.add('', ['foo', 'bar']) // any[]

// InputButton
gooey.add('', () => alert('hi')) // () => void

// InputSwitch
gooey.add('', true) // boolean

// InputButtonGrid
gooey.add('', [
	[
		{ text: 'foo', onClick: () => alert('foo') },
		{ text: 'bar', onClick: () => alert('bar') },
	],
	[
		{ text: 'baz', onClick: () => alert('baz') },
		{ text: 'qux', onClick: () => alert('qux') },
	],
]) // (() => void)[][]
```

</details>

<br>

The type of the `options` object in the third argument will change depending on the type of input, for example:

```typescript
const countInput = gooey.add('count', 1, {
	min: -1,
	max: 10,
	step: 0.1,
})
```

Because the initial value _(`1`)_ is a **number**, gooey infers the options in the third argument as `NumberInputOptions` — which is why it accepts `min`, `max`, and `step`.

If we pass a **string** instead, it'll infer `TextInputOptions`:

```typescript
const textInput = gooey.add('greeting', 'hello', {
	maxLength: 10,
})
```

This should get you some nice, dynamic intellisense. However, you can always fall back to the more specific adders _(like `addNumber`, `addColor`, etc.)_ if need be.

### `addMany`

The `Folder.addMany` method can be used to create multiple inputs at once.

```typescript
type addMany = <T>(
  target: T,
  options?: Record<keyof T, InputOptions<T>> & {
    exclude?: Array<keyof T>
    include?: Array<keyof T>
  },
) => {
  folders: Folder[];
  inputs: Input<T>[];
}
```

It takes in any object, and generates a set of inputs based on the object's keys and values.

Nested objects will result in child folders being created.

Options can be passed to the second argument to customize the inputs being generated, and/or to include/exclude specific keys from generation.

While the simplified version of the type signature for `addMany` above might seem a bit complex, it's actually quite simple in practice! Let's break it down:

The `addMany` method takes two arguments:

1. `target`: The object to create inputs from.
2. `options`: Options to customize the inputs generated, as well as `include` and `exclude` arrays to omit certain keys.

It returns an object with two properties:

1. `folders`: An array of `Folder` instances created from the object's nested objects, if any.
2. `inputs`: An array of `Input` instances created from the object's primitive values.

Let's look at an example to see how this works in practice.

```typescript
const {inputs, folders} = gooey.addMany({
  myNumber: 5,
  myFolder: {
    myColor: '#4aa7ff',
  }
})
```
This will result in an `InputNumber`, and a `Folder` titled `myFolder` containing an `InputColor`.

```typescript
inputs.myNumber  // -> InputNumber
inputs.myColor   // -> InputColor

folders.myFolder // -> Folder
```

Suppose we want to configure the `min` and `max` options for `myNumber`.  To do this, we can specify them in the second argument:

```typescript
const { inputs, folders }  = gooey.addMany({
  myNumber: 5,
  myFolder: {
    myColor: '#4aa7ff',
  }
}, {
  myNumber: {
    min: 0,
    max: 10,
  }
})
```

And that's it!  If all goes well, you should get strong intellisense for all available options in the second argument.  If you don't, please file an issue!

Sometimes, relying on inference won't be enough, and you'll need an escape-hatch to get the exact inputs you want.  In that case, you can `exclude` a key from generation, and create it manually with a more specific adder:

```typescript
const { inputs, folders }  = gooey.addMany({
  myNumber: 5,
  myFolder: {
    myColor: 'hsl(200, 100%, 50%)', // -> InputText (wrong! let's exclude it)
  }
}, {
  exclude: ['myColor'],
})

// ...and now we can add it manually:
gooey.addColor('myColor', 'hsl(200, 100%, 50%)', {
  // and customize it a bit:
  mode: 'hsl'
})
```

### `bind`

```typescript
type bind = <T>(
  target: T,
  key: keyof T,
  options?: InputOptions<T>
): Input<T>
```

The `Folder.bind` method can be used to create an input that is bound to a key on a target object. When an input created with `bind` is changed, the target object's value for the given key will be updated automatically.

```typescript
const data = {
	size: 12,
	color: '#4aa7ff' as const,
}

gooey.bind(data, 'size') // -> InputNumber
gooey.bind(data, 'color') // -> InputColor
```

<br>

## In an app

The constructor touches `document.body` — construct after mount, and `dispose()` on teardown:

```typescript
onMount(() => { gui = new Gooey({ title: 'voice' }) })
onDestroy(() => gui?.dispose())
```

`disabled` and `hidden` take a function, re-evaluated on `input.refresh()` — call it on the dependents when the driver changes:

```typescript
const voice = gui.addSelect('voice', 'charlotte', { options: voices })
const knob = gui.add('stability', 0.5, { disabled: () => !isEleven(voice.value) })
voice.on('change', () => knob.refresh())
```

`input.set(v)` fires `change`; `input.refresh()` re-reads the binding and emits only `refresh` — the path for an update you don't want echoed to your own change handler.

`storage: true` persists `closed`, `theme`, and `presets`; `position` and `size` are opt-in (`storage: { position: true }`); `hidden` is never persisted.

The select dropdown portals to `<body>` at `z-index: 100` — a host panel at or above that hides its own open dropdowns.

`registerWebMCP(gui)` registers one WebMCP tool per input plus a `<prefix>.state` reader, and unregisters on `dispose()`.

<br>

## About

I built this to scratch an itch, and to pave the way for more advanced features related to WebGL / WebAudio / audio-reactive 3D in the future.

[tweakpane](https://github.com/cocopon/tweakpane) was the main inspiration for this project. I recommend it over `gooey` -- it's a more lightweight solution with more features and an awesome, highly active developer!

Other, similar projects:

-   [lil-gui](https://github.com/georgealways/lil-gui)
-   [dat.gui](https://github.com/dataarts/dat.gui)

<br>

## Roadmap

-   [ ] Graph / Monitor Input
-   [ ] LFO / Envelope Manager
-   [ ] Bezier Curve Editor Input
-   [ ] Plugins
-   [ ] Framework Wrappers (svelte 5 runes "just work", but other frameworks need wrappers)

## Classes

### Color

A color class with rgb, hsl, hsv, and kelvin color objects, strings, and conversion methods.

#### Constructors

##### Constructor

> **new Color**(`color?`): [`Color`](#color)

###### Parameters

###### color?

`string` & `object` \| [`ColorValue`](#colorvalue-1)

The initial color value.
The value can be any valid color representation:
- A hex string: '#5500ee' | '#5500eeff'
- An rgba string: 'rgba(85, 0, 238, 1)' | 'rgba(85, 0, 238, 1.0)'
- An hsla string: 'hsla(261, 100%, 47%, 1)' | 'hsla(261, 100%, 47%, 1.0)'
- An RgbvColor: { r: 85, g: 0, b: 238, a: 1 }
- An HsvColor: { h: 261, s: 100, v: 47, a: 1 }
- An HslColor: { h: 261, s: 100, l: 47, a: 1 }
- An KelvinColor: { kelvin: 6500 }

###### Returns

[`Color`](#color)

#### Properties

##### isColor

> `readonly` **isColor**: `true`

***

### Folder

Folder is a container for organizing and grouping Input\|Inputs and child Folders.

This class should not be instantiated directly.  Instead, use the [Gooey.addFolder](#addfolder-1) and
[Folder.addFolder](#addfolder) methods.

#### Example

```typescript
const gooey = new Gooey()
const folder = gooey.addFolder({ title: 'My Folder' })
folder.addNumber({ title: 'foo', value: 5 })
```

#### Constructors

##### Constructor

> **new Folder**(`options`): [`Folder`](#folder)

###### Parameters

###### options

`FolderOptions`

###### Returns

[`Folder`](#folder)

#### Properties

##### \_\_type

> **\_\_type**: `"Folder"`

##### children

> **children**: [`Folder`](#folder)[]

The child folders of this folder.

##### closed

> **closed**: `UnionState`\<`boolean`\>

An observable responsible for the folder's open/closed state.  Setting this value will
open/close the folder, and subscribing to this value will allow you to listen for
open/close events.

##### disposed

> **disposed**: `boolean` = `false`

##### element

> **element**: `HTMLDivElement`

The folder's root container element, containing all other related folder [elements](#elements).

##### elements

> **elements**: `object`

All HTMLElements that make up the folder's UI.

###### content

> **content**: `HTMLElement`

###### contentWrapper

> **contentWrapper**: `HTMLElement`

###### header

> **header**: `HTMLElement`

> **title**: `HTMLElement`

> **container**: `HTMLElement`

The animated svg graphics belonging to the folder.

> **container**: `HTMLDivElement`

> **id**: `string`

##### inputs

> **inputs**: `Map`\<`string`, `ValidInput`\>

All inputs added to this folder.

##### isRoot

> **isRoot**: `boolean` = `true`

##### on

> **on**: \<`K`\>(`event`, `callback`) => `string`

Equivalent to `addEventListener`.

Register a new event listener.

###### Type Parameters

###### K

`K` *extends* keyof `FolderEvents`

###### Parameters

###### event

`K`

The name of the event to listen for.

###### callback

`EventCallback`\<`FolderEvents`\[`K`\]\>

The callback function to execute when the event is fired.

###### Returns

`string`

The ID of the listener (for use via unlisten to remove the listener).

##### parentFolder

> **parentFolder**: [`Folder`](#folder)

The parent folder of this folder (or a circular reference if this is the root folder).

##### presetId

> **presetId**: `string`

A preset namespace to use for saving/loading.  By default, the [\`title\`](#title)
is used, in combiniation with the parent folder's title (and so on up the hierarchy).
Therefore, if you want to use presets, you will only need to set this if you:
- Use the same title for multiple inputs _in the same [Folder](#folder)_, or
- Leave all titles empty
Otherwise, this can be left as the default and presets will work as expected.

###### Default

The provided `title`.

##### root

> **root**: [`Folder`](#folder)

The root folder.  All folders share a reference to the same root folder.

##### saveable

> **saveable**: `boolean`

Whether this Folder should be saved as a FolderPreset when saving the
[GooeyPreset](#gooeypreset) for the [Gooey](#gooey-1) this Folder belongs to.  If `false`, this Input will
be skipped.

###### Default

```ts
true
```

##### settingsFolder

> **settingsFolder**: [`Folder`](#folder)

The folder containing Gooey instance settings, like the `ui` and `presets` sections.

##### addElement()

> **addElement**(`title`, `content`, `options?`): [`InputElement`](#inputelement)

Adds a new [InputElement](#inputelement) to the folder, mounting arbitrary content in place of a
controller.  The content is either an existing element, or a mount function receiving the
container (and optionally returning a cleanup function).  It has no value to serialize, so
it's skipped when saving and loading presets.

###### Parameters

###### title

`string`

###### content

[`ElementContent`](#elementcontent)

###### options?

`Partial`\<[`ElementInputOptions`](#elementinputoptions)\>

###### Returns

[`InputElement`](#inputelement)

###### Example

```ts
gui.addElement('Notes', container => {
	container.innerHTML = renderMarkdown(notes)
	return () => container.replaceChildren()
})
```

##### addMany()

> **addMany**\<`T`, `TOptions`, `TInputs`\>(`target`, `options?`): `object`

Takes an object and generates a set of inputs based on the object's keys and values.  Any
nested objects will result in child folders being created.  Options can be passed to
customize the inputs generated, and to exclude/include specific keys.

###### Type Parameters

###### T

`T` *extends* `object`

###### TOptions

`TOptions` *extends* `InferTargetOptions`\<`T`\> = `InferTargetOptions`\<`T`\>

###### TInputs

`TInputs` *extends* `object` = `InferInputs`\<`T`\>

###### Parameters

###### target

`T`

The object to generate inputs from.

###### options?

`TOptions` & `object`

Options to customize the inputs generated, as well as `include` and
`exclude` arrays to omit certain keys.

###### Returns

`object`

###### folders

> **folders**: `InferFolders`\<`T`\>

###### inputs

> **inputs**: `TInputs`

###### Example

```ts
const gui = new Gooey()

const params = {
 myNumber: 5,
	myFolder: {
   myOptions: 'foo',
	}
}

gui.addMany(params, {
  myFolder: {
folderOptions: title: 'My Folder' }}, // optional folder controls
})

##### addNumber()

> **addNumber**(`title`, `value?`, `options?`): [`InputNumber`](#inputnumber)

Adds a new [InputNumber](#inputnumber) to the folder.

###### Parameters

###### title

`string`

###### value?

`number`

###### options?

`Partial`\<[`NumberInputOptions`](#numberinputoptions)\> = `...`

###### Returns

[`InputNumber`](#inputnumber)

###### Example

```ts
const number = gui.addNumber('Foo', true)
number.on('change', console.log)
```

##### addSelect()

> **addSelect**\<`T`\>(`title`, `valueOrConfig`, `options?`): [`InputSelect`](#inputselect)\<`T`\>

Adds a new [InputSelect](#inputselect) to the folder.

###### Type Parameters

###### T

`T`

###### Parameters

###### title

`string`

###### valueOrConfig

`T` \| \{ `options`: `Option`\<`T`\>[]; `value`: `T`; \}

###### options?

`Omit`\<`InputOptions`\<`NoInfer`\<`T`\> \| \{ `label`: `string`; `value`: `NoInfer`\<`T`\>; \}\>, `"onChange"`\> & `object` & `object`

###### Returns

[`InputSelect`](#inputselect)\<`T`\>

###### Example

```ts
// Pattern 1: Value first, options in config (consistent with other inputs)
gui.addSelect('theme', 'light', { options: ['light', 'dark'] })

// Pattern 2: Inline value+options object (skip 3rd param, works great with addMany)
gui.addSelect('theme', { value: 'light', options: ['light', 'dark'] })

// Pattern 3: Labeled options (for non-primitives needing labels)
gui.addSelect('item', { value: 1, options: [{ value: 1, label: 'One' }, { value: 2, label: 'Two' }] })
```

##### bind()

> **bind**\<`TTarget`, `TKey`, `TValue`, `TOptions`, `TInput`\>(`target`, `key`, `options?`): `TInput`

Binds an input to a target object and key.  The input will automatically update the target
object's key when the input value changes.

###### Type Parameters

###### TTarget

`TTarget` *extends* `Record`\<`string`, `any`\>

###### TKey

`TKey` *extends* `string` \| `number` \| `symbol`

###### TValue

`TValue` *extends* `any`

###### TOptions

`TOptions` *extends* [`TextInputOptions`](#textinputoptions) \| [`NumberInputOptions`](#numberinputoptions) \| [`ColorInputOptions`](#colorinputoptions) \| [`SelectInputOptions`](#selectinputoptions)\<`any`\> \| [`SwitchInputOptions`](#switchinputoptions) \| [`SelectInputOptions`](#selectinputoptions)\<`unknown`\>

###### TInput

`TInput` *extends* [`InputText`](#inputtext) \| [`InputNumber`](#inputnumber) \| [`InputColor`](#inputcolor) \| [`InputButton`](#inputbutton) \| [`InputSwitch`](#inputswitch) \| [`InputSelect`](#inputselect)\<`unknown`\> \| [`InputSelect`](#inputselect)\<`any`\>

###### Parameters

###### target

`TTarget`

The object to bind the input to.

###### key

`TKey`

The key of the target object to bind the input to.

###### options?

`Partial`\<`TOptions`\> = `{}`

The InputOptions, the type of which is inferred based on the type
of the value at the target object's key.

###### Returns

`TInput`

###### Example

```ts
const gui = new Gooey()

// Some state.
const params = { foo: 5, bar: 'baz', qux: true }

const numberInput = gui.bind(params, 'foo', { min: 0, max: 10, step: 1 })
//    ^? InputNumber

// By default, the `title` is inferred from the key.
// To override it, use the `title` option:
const switchInput = gui.bind(params, 'qux', { title: 'Kwucks' })
```

##### addElement()

> **addElement**(`title`, `content`, `options?`): [`InputElement`](#inputelement)

Adds a new [InputElement](#inputelement) to the folder, mounting arbitrary content in place of a
controller.  The content is either an existing element, or a mount function receiving the
container (and optionally returning a cleanup function).  It has no value to serialize, so
it's skipped when saving and loading presets.

###### Parameters

###### title

`string`

###### content

[`ElementContent`](#elementcontent)

###### options?

`Partial`\<[`ElementInputOptions`](#elementinputoptions)\>

###### Returns

[`InputElement`](#inputelement)

###### Example

```ts
gui.addElement('Notes', container => {
	container.innerHTML = renderMarkdown(notes)
	return () => container.replaceChildren()
})
```

###### Inherited from

[`Folder`](#folder).[`addElement`](#addelement)

##### addMany()

> **addMany**\<`T`, `TOptions`, `TInputs`\>(`target`, `options?`): `object`

Takes an object and generates a set of inputs based on the object's keys and values.  Any
nested objects will result in child folders being created.  Options can be passed to
customize the inputs generated, and to exclude/include specific keys.

###### Type Parameters

###### T

`T` *extends* `object`

###### TOptions

`TOptions` *extends* `InferTargetOptions`\<`T`\> = `InferTargetOptions`\<`T`\>

###### TInputs

`TInputs` *extends* `object` = `InferInputs`\<`T`\>

###### Parameters

###### target

`T`

The object to generate inputs from.

###### options?

`TOptions` & `object`

Options to customize the inputs generated, as well as `include` and
`exclude` arrays to omit certain keys.

###### Returns

`object`

###### folders

> **folders**: `InferFolders`\<`T`\>

###### inputs

> **inputs**: `TInputs`

###### Example

```ts
const gui = new Gooey()

const params = {
 myNumber: 5,
	myFolder: {
   myOptions: 'foo',
	}
}

gui.addMany(params, {
  myFolder: {
folderOptions: title: 'My Folder' }}, // optional folder controls
})

###### Inherited from

`Pick.addMany`

##### addSelect()

> **addSelect**\<`T`\>(`title`, `valueOrConfig`, `options?`): [`InputSelect`](#inputselect)\<`T`\>

Adds a new [InputSelect](#inputselect) to the folder.

###### Type Parameters

###### T

`T`

###### Parameters

###### title

`string`

###### valueOrConfig

`T` \| \{ `options`: `Option`\<`T`\>[]; `value`: `T`; \}

###### options?

`Omit`\<`InputOptions`\<`NoInfer`\<`T`\> \| \{ `label`: `string`; `value`: `NoInfer`\<`T`\>; \}\>, `"onChange"`\> & `object` & `object`

###### Returns

[`InputSelect`](#inputselect)\<`T`\>

###### Example

```ts
// Pattern 1: Value first, options in config (consistent with other inputs)
gui.addSelect('theme', 'light', { options: ['light', 'dark'] })

// Pattern 2: Inline value+options object (skip 3rd param, works great with addMany)
gui.addSelect('theme', { value: 'light', options: ['light', 'dark'] })

// Pattern 3: Labeled options (for non-primitives needing labels)
gui.addSelect('item', { value: 1, options: [{ value: 1, label: 'One' }, { value: 2, label: 'Two' }] })
```

###### Inherited from

`Pick.addSelect`

##### bind()

> **bind**\<`TTarget`, `TKey`, `TValue`, `TOptions`, `TInput`\>(`target`, `key`, `options?`): `TInput`

Binds an input to a target object and key.  The input will automatically update the target
object's key when the input value changes.

###### Type Parameters

###### TTarget

`TTarget` *extends* `Record`\<`string`, `any`\>

###### TKey

`TKey` *extends* `string` \| `number` \| `symbol`

###### TValue

`TValue` *extends* `any`

###### TOptions

`TOptions` *extends* [`TextInputOptions`](#textinputoptions) \| [`NumberInputOptions`](#numberinputoptions) \| [`ColorInputOptions`](#colorinputoptions) \| [`SelectInputOptions`](#selectinputoptions)\<`any`\> \| [`SwitchInputOptions`](#switchinputoptions) \| [`SelectInputOptions`](#selectinputoptions)\<`unknown`\>

###### TInput

`TInput` *extends* [`InputText`](#inputtext) \| [`InputNumber`](#inputnumber) \| [`InputColor`](#inputcolor) \| [`InputButton`](#inputbutton) \| [`InputSwitch`](#inputswitch) \| [`InputSelect`](#inputselect)\<`unknown`\> \| [`InputSelect`](#inputselect)\<`any`\>

###### Parameters

###### target

`TTarget`

The object to bind the input to.

###### key

`TKey`

The key of the target object to bind the input to.

###### options?

`Partial`\<`TOptions`\> = `{}`

The InputOptions, the type of which is inferred based on the type
of the value at the target object's key.

###### Returns

`TInput`

###### Example

```ts
const gui = new Gooey()

// Some state.
const params = { foo: 5, bar: 'baz', qux: true }

const numberInput = gui.bind(params, 'foo', { min: 0, max: 10, step: 1 })
//    ^? InputNumber

// By default, the `title` is inferred from the key.
// To override it, use the `title` option:
const switchInput = gui.bind(params, 'qux', { title: 'Kwucks' })
```

###### Inherited from

`Pick.bind`

### WindowManager

Manages multiple draggable and/or resizable [WindowInstance](#windowinstance)s.

[\`windows\`](#windows) can be added, removed, and their
z-index values are managed to ensure the most recently selected element is on top.

### GooeyOptions

#### Properties

##### \_\_type

> **\_\_type**: `"GooeyOptions"`

##### closed

> **closed**: `boolean`

The initial expanded state of the gooey.

###### Default

```ts
false
```

##### container

> **container**: `string` \| `HTMLElement`

The container to append the gooey to.

###### Default

```ts
'body'
```

##### defaultPreset?

> `optional` **defaultPreset?**: [`GooeyPreset`](#gooeypreset)

The default preset to load when the gooey is created, or the initial gooey state if undefined.

###### Default

```ts
undefined
```

##### draggable

> **draggable**: `boolean`

Whether the gooey is draggable.

###### Default

```ts
true
```

##### hidden?

> `optional` **hidden?**: `boolean`

The initial hidden state of the gooey.

###### Default

```ts
false
```

##### id?

> `optional` **id?**: `string`

A unique id for the gooey's root element.

###### Default

nanoid

##### loadDefaultFont?

> `optional` **loadDefaultFont?**: `boolean`

Whether to load the default font for use.  Set to `false` if you're overwriting
the `--gooey-font-family` variable in your theme.

###### Default

```ts
true
```

##### margin

> **margin**: `number` \| \{ `x?`: `number`; `y?`: `number`; \}

The margin in pixels to apply to the placement.  Can be a number
to apply the same margin to both x and y, or an object with x
and y properties to apply different margins to each axis.

###### Default

```ts
16
```

##### maxHeight?

> `optional` **maxHeight?**: `string` \| `number`

The tallest the gooey's content may grow before it scrolls, as a css `max-height` on the
root content element.  A number is pixels, a string is passed through as a css length
(`'90vh'`), and `'none'` leaves it unbounded.

###### Remarks

This caps the scrolling content, not the header -- the root itself is
`height: fit-content`, and the resize grabbers are left/right only.  Writes the
`--gooey-root_max-height` custom property inline on `.gooey-root`, so it survives a theme or
mode change.  When omitted, the `:where(.gooey-root)` default in `gooey.scss` (`90vh`)
applies.

###### Default

```ts
undefined
```

##### maxWidth?

> `optional` **maxWidth?**: `string` \| `number`

The widest the gooey may be, as a resize ceiling and a css `max-width` on
[Gooey.element](#element-1).  A number is pixels, a string is passed through as a css length, and
`'none'` leaves it unbounded -- which is what a gooey used as a window rather than a control
panel usually wants, since the default `35rem` silently stops a drag at 560px.

###### Remarks

Writes the `--gooey-root_max-width` custom property inline on `.gooey-root`, so it
survives a theme or mode change.  When omitted, the `:where(.gooey-root)` default in
`gooey.scss` (`35rem`) applies.

###### Default

```ts
undefined
```

##### minWidth?

> `optional` **minWidth?**: `string` \| `number`

The narrowest the gooey may be, as a resize floor and a css `min-width` on
[Gooey.element](#element-1).  A number is pixels, a string is passed through as a css length
(`'12rem'`, `'30%'`), and `'none'` leaves it unbounded.

###### Remarks

Writes the `--gooey-root_min-width` custom property inline on `.gooey-root`, so it
survives a theme or mode change.  When omitted, the `:where(.gooey-root)` default in
`gooey.scss` (`20rem`) applies.

###### Default

```ts
undefined
```

##### offset?

> `optional` **offset?**: `object`

An offset to apply to the initial position of the gooey.

###### x?

> `optional` **x?**: `number`

###### y?

> `optional` **y?**: `number`

###### Default

```ts
{ x: 0, y: 0 }
```

##### parentGooey?

> `optional` **parentGooey?**: [`Gooey`](#gooey-1)

Another [Gooey](#gooey-1) to share a [WindowManager](#windowmanager-1) and Themer with.  Child
gooeys stack against their parent instead of floating in a z-order of their own, and
follow its theme.  Each still keeps its own [storage](#storage) key, so
position and size persist per window.

Disposing a child leaves the parent's window manager and themer alone.

###### Default

```ts
undefined
```

##### position

> **position**: `Placement` \| \{ `x`: `number`; `y`: `number`; \}

The gooey's initial position on the screen.  If `undefined`, the gooey will
be placed in the top-right corner of the screen.

This value can either be a Placement string, or an object with
`x` and `y` properties representing the position in pixels.

###### Default

```ts
'top-right'
```

##### presets?

> `optional` **presets?**: [`GooeyPreset`](#gooeypreset)[]

Presets to make available in the gooey.

###### Default

```ts
[]
```

##### resizable

> **resizable**: `boolean`

Whether the gooey is resizable.

###### Default

```ts
true
```

##### settingsFolder?

> `optional` **settingsFolder?**: `false` \| `Partial`\<`FolderOptions`\> & `object`

Any FolderOptions for the builtin global settings folder.  It also accepts 2
additional settings, `uiFolder` and `presetsFolder`, which are FolderOptions
for the 2 sub-folders.

###### Default

`false` hides the settings folder and omits the toolbar's settings button, for a gooey
used as a plain window rather than a control panel.  The folder itself is still built, so
the [themer](#themer) and [preset manager](#presetmanager) behave
exactly as they otherwise would -- there is simply no way in.

##### storage

> **storage**: `boolean` \| `Partial`\<[`GooeyStorageOptions`](#gooeystorageoptions)\>

Defines which properties to persist in localStorage, and under which
key, if any.  If `true`, the [GUI\_STORAGE\_DEFAULTS](#gui_storage_defaults) will be used.
If `false`, no state will be persisted.

###### Default

```ts
true
```

##### theme

> **theme**: `GooeyTheme`

The title of the theme to use for the gooey.  To add your own themes,
use [themes](#themes).  Ignored under [parentGooey](#parentgooey) — a child
follows the parent's theme.

###### Default

```ts
'vanilla'
```

##### themeMode

> **themeMode**: `"light"` \| `"dark"` \| `"system"`

The initial Themer.mode\|theme mode.

###### Default

```ts
'dark'
```

##### themes

> **themes**: `Theme`[]

The themes available to the gooey.

###### Default Value

[ theme\_default\|default, theme\_flat\|flat, theme\_scout\|scout ]

##### title

> **title**: `string`

The title of the Gooey.

###### Default

```ts
'gooey'
```

##### width?

> `optional` **width?**: `number`

The initial width of the gooey in pixels.

###### Remarks

This can also be set by overriding the `--gooey-root_width` CSS custom property on
the [Gooey.element](#element-1) element `.gooey-root`, which is responsible for the root width.

A [minWidth](#minwidth-1) / [maxWidth](#maxwidth-1) given
explicitly wins over this.  Without one, a `width` below the default minimum lowers that
minimum so the gooey can actually be as narrow as it was asked to be.

###### Default

```ts
undefined
```

> **\_\_version**: `string` \| `number`

### GooeyStorageOptions

Defines which properties to persist in localStorage, and under which
key.

#### Example

```ts
// defaults:
{
  key: 'gooey',
  closed: true,
  theme: true,
  presets: true,
  position: false,
  size: false,
}
```

#### Properties

##### \_\_type

> **\_\_type**: `"GooeyStorageOptions"`

##### closed?

> `optional` **closed?**: `boolean`

Whether to persist the folder's expanded state.

###### Default

```ts
true
```

##### key

> **key**: `string`

Prefix to use for localStorage keys.

###### Remarks

The provided string is prepended to the gooey's title, lowercased, and hyphens
are replaced with spaces.  For example, a gooey titled `"Foo Bar"` is stored as
`"foo-bar::gooey"`.

###### Default

```ts
"default"
```

##### position?

> `optional` **position?**: `boolean`

Whether to persist the gooey's position.

###### Default

```ts
false
```

##### presets?

> `optional` **presets?**: `boolean`

Whether to persist the gooey's presets.

###### Default

```ts
true
```

##### size?

> `optional` **size?**: `boolean`

Whether to persist the gooey's size.

###### Default

```ts
false
```

##### theme?

> `optional` **theme?**: `boolean`

Whether to persist the theme.

###### Default

```ts
true
```

***

### InputArray

#### Extends

- `Input`\<`T`[], [`ArrayInputOptions`](#arrayinputoptions)\<`T`\>, `ArrayControllerElements`\>

#### Type Parameters

##### T

`T` = `any`

#### Properties

##### \_\_type

##### listen

> **listen**: \<`TTarget`, `TEventName`, `TEventInstance`\>(`element`, `event`, `callback`, `options?`, `groupId?`) => `string`

Add an event listener to an HTMLElement that will be removed when [dispose](#dispose-5) is called.

###### Type Parameters

###### TTarget

`TTarget` *extends* `Element` \| `Window` \| `Document`

###### TEventName

`TEventName` *extends* `string` & `object` \| keyof GlobalEventHandlersEventMap

###### TEventInstance

`TEventInstance` *extends* `Event` \| (Event \| ProgressEvent\<EventTarget\> \| UIEvent \| AnimationEvent \| PointerEvent \| MouseEvent \| ... 13 more ... \| WheelEvent) & \{ ...; \}

###### Parameters

###### element

`TTarget`

The element to add the listener to.

###### event

`TEventName`

The event to listen for.

###### callback

(`e`) => `void`

The callback function to execute when the event is fired.

###### options?

`AddEventListenerOptions`

Optional event listener options.

###### groupId?

`string`

Optional group ID to add the listener to (for batch removal).

###### Returns

`string`

###### Inherited from

`Input.listen`

##### on

> **on**: \<`K`\>(`event`, `callback`) => `string`

Register a new event listener.

###### Type Parameters

###### K

`K` *extends* keyof `InputEvents`\<`T`[]\>

###### Parameters

###### event

`K`

The name of the event to listen for.

###### callback

`EventCallback`\<`InputEvents`\<`T`[]\>\[`K`\]\>

The callback function to execute when the event is fired.

###### Returns

`string`

The ID of the listener (for use via unlisten to remove the listener).

###### Inherited from

`Input.on`

##### opts

### InputElement

An input that mounts arbitrary content in its content area instead of a controller.  Use it to
put consumer-rendered DOM -- a chart, a markdown card, a preview -- in a folder alongside normal
inputs.  It has no value to serialize, so it opts out of presets by default.

#### Example

```ts
const card = gooey.addElement('Notes', container => {
	container.innerHTML = renderMarkdown(notes)
	return () => container.replaceChildren()
})

card.set(someOtherElement)
```

#### Extends

- `Input`\<[`ElementContent`](#elementcontent), [`ElementInputOptions`](#elementinputoptions), `ElementControllerElements`\>

#### Properties

### InputNumber

A combined input with a traditional text input, increment/decrement buttons, and a slider.

#### Example

```ts
gooey.add('foo', 0)
gooey.addNumber('bar', 10)
gooey.bind({ baz: 100 }, 'baz')
```

Hold down `cmd`/`ctrl` to snap to drag the number text input.

Hold down `shift` to double the step, and `option`/`alt` to halve it (this works both on the slider, and when dragging the text input).

#### Extends

- `Input`\<`number`, [`NumberInputOptions`](#numberinputoptions), `NumberControllerElements`\>

#### Properties

##### \_\_type

> `readonly` **\_\_type**: `"InputNumber"`

###### Overrides

`Input.__type`

##### bound

> **bound**: `boolean` = `false`

Whether the input was initialized with a bind target/key.

###### Default

```ts
false
```

###### labelKey?

> `optional` **labelKey?**: `TValueType` *extends* `Record`\<`K`, `any`\> ? `K` : `string`

For arrays of unlabeled objects, labelKey specifies a key to use as the label.
If none is provided, select will attempt to use a `label` or `title` key if they exist.
If neither exist, an error will be thrown.

##### selected

> **selected**: `PrimitiveState`\<`LabeledOption`\<`TValueType`\>\>

The currently selected option (full LabeledOption<T> with both label and value).
This is the source of truth for the selection. When this changes, `state` is
automatically updated with the raw value.

##### state

> **state**: [`State`](#state-9)\<`TValueType`\>

Reactive state containing the raw value (T, not LabeledOption<T>).
This is automatically kept in sync with `selected`.
Consistent with other Input types.

##### listen

> **listen**: \<`TTarget`, `TEventName`, `TEventInstance`\>(`element`, `event`, `callback`, `options?`, `groupId?`) => `string`

Add an event listener to an HTMLElement that will be removed when [dispose](#dispose-13) is called.

###### Type Parameters

###### TTarget

`TTarget` *extends* `Element` \| `Window` \| `Document`

###### TEventName

`TEventName` *extends* `string` & `object` \| keyof GlobalEventHandlersEventMap

###### TEventInstance

`TEventInstance` *extends* `Event` \| (Event \| ProgressEvent\<EventTarget\> \| UIEvent \| AnimationEvent \| PointerEvent \| MouseEvent \| ... 13 more ... \| WheelEvent) & \{ ...; \}

###### Parameters

###### element

`TTarget`

The element to add the listener to.

###### event

`TEventName`

The event to listen for.

###### callback

(`e`) => `void`

The callback function to execute when the event is fired.

###### options?

`AddEventListenerOptions`

Optional event listener options.

###### groupId?

`string`

Optional group ID to add the listener to (for batch removal).

###### Returns

`string`

###### Inherited from

`Input.listen`

##### on

> **on**: \<`K`\>(`event`, `callback`) => `string`

###### Type Parameters

###### K

###### Parameters

###### event

`K`

###### callback

`EventCallback`\<`InputEvents`\<`string`\>\[`K`\]\>

###### Returns

`string`

### TooltipOptions

Options for a single instance of the [Tooltip](#tooltip) class.

#### Properties

##### \_\_type?

> `readonly` `optional` **\_\_type?**: `"TooltipOptions"`

##### anchor

> **anchor**: `Anchor` \| `Anchors`

The element to which the tooltip is placed relative to.  Can be a selector,
an element, or the string literal `'mouse'` to use the pointer position.

Can also be an object with unique `x` and `y` anchors for each axis.

By default, the node that the tooltip is attached to will be used as the anchor.

###### Example

```ts
{ x: 'mouse', y: undefined }
```

##### animation

> **animation**: `object`

Animation in/out duration times / easing.

###### duration

> **duration**: `string` \| `number` \| `CSSNumericValue` \| `undefined`

The tooltip reveal animation duration in ms.

###### Default Value

```ts
300
```

###### durationOut

> **durationOut**: `string` \| `number` \| `CSSNumericValue` \| `undefined`

The tooltip hide animation duration in ms.

###### Default Value

```ts
150
```

###### easing

> **easing**: `string` \| `undefined`

The tooltip reveal and hide animation easing.

###### Default Value

```ts
'cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.320, 1)'
```

##### delay

> **delay**: `number`

Delay in milliseconds before the tooltip is shown.

###### Default Value

```ts
250
```

##### delayOut

> **delayOut**: `number`

Delay in milliseconds before the tooltip is hidden.

###### Default Value

```ts
50
```

##### hideOnClick

> **hideOnClick**: `boolean`

Hides the tooltip on click if `true`.

###### Default Value

```ts
false
```

##### manual?

> `optional` **manual?**: `boolean`

If `true`, the tooltip will not be shown automatically and must be controlled manually with
the [Tooltip.show](#show-2) and [Tooltip.hide](#hide-2) methods.

###### Default Value

```ts
false
```

##### offsetX

> **offsetX**: `string`

An optional x-axis offset (any valid css unit).

###### Default Value

```ts
'0%'
```

##### offsetY

> **offsetY**: `string`

An optional y-axis offset (any valid css unit).

###### Default Value

```ts
'0%'
```

##### parent?

> `optional` **parent?**: `HTMLElement`

If specified, the container element for the tooltip.

###### Default Value

```ts
document.body
```

##### placement

> **placement**: `"top"` \| `"right"` \| `"bottom"` \| `"left"`

The placement of the tooltip relative to the element.  Can be `'top'`, `'bottom'`, `'left'`, or `'right'`.

##### style?

> `optional` **style?**: `Partial`\<`Record`\<keyof PropertiesHyphen\<0 \| (string & \{\}), string & \{\}\> \| `` `--${string}` ``, `string`\>\> \| (() => `StyleDefinition`)

Custom style overrides for the tooltip element (all valid CSS properties are allowed).
i.e. { 'background-color': 'red' }
For dynamic styles, you can provide a function that returns the overrides instead, and
it will be called before the tooltip is shown and apply any changes to the tooltip.

###### Default Value

```ts
undefined
```

##### text

> **text**: `string` \| (() => `string`)

The text to display in the tooltip.  Can be a string, number, or a function that returns a string or number.

##### tools

###### Returns

`void`

###### Returns

`void`

### WebMCPTool

The subset of a WebMCP tool declaration that gooey produces.

WebMCP is a
[Community Group draft](https://webmachinelearning.github.io/webmcp/|W3C) and ships behind
a Chrome origin trial, so the DOM lib has no types for it yet.  These declarations are
deliberately minimal -- just enough to call `registerTool` -- and are not a global augmentation,
so they can't conflict with the real thing once browsers ship it.

#### Properties

##### description

> **description**: `string`

A one-line, human-readable explanation of what calling the tool does.

##### execute

> **execute**: (`args`) => `string` \| `Promise`\<`string`\>

Runs the tool and returns a string result for the agent.

###### Parameters

###### args

`Record`\<`string`, `unknown`\>

###### Returns

`string` \| `Promise`\<`string`\>

##### inputSchema

> **inputSchema**: [`WebMCPInputSchema`](#webmcpinputschema)

A JSON Schema describing the tool's argument object.

##### name

> **name**: `string`

A unique, stable identifier the agent calls.

***

### State

> **State**\<`T`\> = `IsUnion`\<`T`\> *extends* `true` ? `UnionState`\<`T`\> : `T` *extends* infer U[] ? `ArrayState`\<`U`\> : `T` *extends* `Map`\<infer K, infer V\> ? `MapState`\<`K`, `V`\> : `T` *extends* `Set`\<infer U\> ? `SetState`\<`U`\> : `PrimitiveState`\<`T`\>

A state store is a traditional observable store with additional methods for Arrays, Maps, Sets,
getting and setting the value, reacting to changes, and easily persisting to local storage.

#### Type Parameters

##### T

`T`

#### Param

**set**

Sets the value of the store.

#### Param

**update**

Provides the current value, and updates it to the returned value.

#### Param

**subscribe**

Subscribes to the store.

#### Param

**get**

Returns the current value of the store.

#### Param

**refresh**

Refreshes the store.

#### Param

**onChange**

Adds a callback that runs when the store changes.

#### Param

**destroy**

Destroys the store and cleans up all listeners.

#### Param

**isState**

Whether this is a state store.
todo - A `subscribeOnce` or `subscribeFor` could be nice.

***

### WindowInstanceOptions

> **WindowInstanceOptions** = `Partial`\<[`WindowManagerOptions`](#windowmanageroptions)\> & `object`

#### Type Declaration

##### id?

> `optional` **id?**: `string`

A unique identifier for the window, making it accessible via the
[\`windows\`](#windows) map (i.e. `windowManager.windows.get(id)`).

If not provided, a random id will be generated.

###### Default

```ts
nanoid()
```

##### storageId?

> `optional` **storageId?**: `string`

A _stable_ identifier used to key this window's persisted position / size in
localStorage.  Unlike id, it must be the same on every page load -- it is the
only way for a window to find its own saved layout again.

Resolution order, highest priority first:

1. this option
2. the `id` attribute already present on the node when it was added
3. the window's insertion index _(fallback)_

The insertion-index fallback is only stable for apps that always create the same
windows in the same order.  If the number or order of windows can vary between page
loads, windows will read each other's saved layouts -- pass a `storageId` (or give the
element an `id`) to avoid it.

###### Remarks

id is deliberately _not_ used, since it's often generated per-session
(i.e. nanoid), which would silently orphan every write.

###### Default

```ts
undefined
```

### registerWebMCP()

> **registerWebMCP**(`gooey`, `options?`): [`WebMCPHandle`](#webmcphandle)

Exposes a [Gooey](#gooey-1)'s controls to in-browser AI agents as
[https://webmachinelearning.github.io/webmcp/\|WebMCP](https://webmachinelearning.github.io/webmcp/|WebMCP) tools -- one setter per input, plus
a `state` tool that reads the whole panel in a single call.  Setters go through each input's own
`set`, so bindings, `onChange` handlers, and undo history behave exactly as they do for a click.

In a browser without `document.modelContext` this registers nothing and returns a disabled
handle.  It never throws, and nothing imports it, so it costs nothing until you call it.

#### Parameters

##### gooey

[`Gooey`](#gooey-1)

##### options?

[`WebMCPOptions`](#webmcpoptions) = `{}`

#### Returns

[`WebMCPHandle`](#webmcphandle)

#### Example

```ts
import { Gooey, registerWebMCP } from 'gooey'

const gooey = new Gooey('Scene')
gooey.addNumber('speed', 1, { min: 0, max: 10 })

const agentDoor = registerWebMCP(gooey)
// → tools: scene.state, scene.speed
```

***

### state()

> **state**\<`T`\>(`defaultValue`, `options?`): [`State`](#state-9)\<`T`\>

An advanced store factory with additional features:

- Support for Maps, Sets, and Arrays (enabling methods like `.push` and `.add`).
- A `.get` method for retrieving the current value of the store.
- Optional `onChange` callback for adding side effects without subscribing.
- Optional `key` argument for persisting the store to local storage.

#### Type Parameters

##### T

`T`

#### Parameters

##### defaultValue

`T`

The default value of the store.

##### options?

`StateOptions`\<`T`\>

StateOptions

#### Returns

[`State`](#state-9)\<`T`\>

#### Example

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
	import { state } from 'fractils'

	const foo = state([1, 2, 3], { key: 'foo' }) // persisted to local storage
	foo.push(4)
	foo.push('5') // Type error

	const bar = state(new Map<string, number>())
	bar.setKey('count', 21) // `set` is taken, so we use `setKey` and `deleteKey`

	const baz = state(new Set<number>())
	baz.add(5)
	baz.push(6) // Type error
</script>

<h1>{$foo} {$bar} {$baz}</h1>
```

***

### tooltip()

> **tooltip**(`node`, `options?`): `object`

A wrapper function that creates a new [Tooltip](#tooltip) instance and returns
an object with `update` and `destroy` methods, compatible with Svelte actions.

#### Parameters

##### node

`HTMLElement`

##### options?

`Partial`\<[`TooltipOptions`](#tooltipoptions)\>

#### Returns

`object`

##### destroy()

> **destroy**(): `void`

###### Returns

`void`

##### update()

> **update**(`opts`): `void`

###### Parameters

###### opts

[`TooltipOptions`](#tooltipoptions)

###### Returns

`void`

#### Examples

**Vanilla**

```js
import { tooltip } from 'lib/actions/tooltip'

const el = document.querySelector('div')
const tip = tooltip(el, { text: 'Hello, world!', placement: 'top' })
```

**Svelte**

```svelte
<script>
	import { tooltip } from 'lib/actions/tooltip'
</script>

<div use:tooltip={{ text: 'Hello, world!', placement: 'top' }}>
	Hover me!
</div>
```
